events.label: CPS discontinued all charges; it said withdrawal of key witnesses plus new material meant no longer a realistic prospect of conviction. No trial or not-guilty verdict took place.
United said its fact-finding phase had ended but its decision was still in final stages; public and supporter debate was prominent.

United announced the result of its own internal inquiry and a mutually agreed departure away from Old Trafford. This was an employer decision, not a court finding. United’s CEO said he made the decision and acknowledged strong opinions and a wish to avoid club distraction.
United announced a season-long loan to Getafe, subject to clearance. This documents the move abroad after the club decision; it does not show the press caused it.

evidence.label: Greater Manchester Police statement announcing CPS discontinuance, 2 February 2023
evidence.text: GMP states proceedings against the 21-year-old man had been discontinued by the CPS. GMP says it made the announcement because of significant media coverage; it says the investigation team had remained in regular contact with the legal team and understood the rationale. This is a discontinuance notice, not a verdict.

evidence.label: CPS discontinuance statement (original CPS page URL; text reproduced by government news syndication)
evidence.text: CPS states one charge each of attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour, and assault occasioning actual bodily harm were discontinued under the Code for Crown Prosecutors. It gave withdrawal of key witnesses plus new material and concluded there was no longer a realistic prospect of conviction. The CPS explicitly notes that it is not its function to decide guilt. No trial or not-guilty verdict followed. Original CPS URL now returns404; the linked page reproduces the CPS statement.

evidence.label: Manchester United official club statement, 21 August 2023
evidence.text: United announced a six-month internal investigation had concluded and that Greenwood would leave by mutual agreement. It said, based on evidence available to the club, it concluded online material did not provide the full picture and he did not commit the acts charged. The club said resuming at United would be difficult and it would work with him on an outcome away from Old Trafford. This was an employer inquiry and employment decision, not a criminal court finding.

evidence.label: Richard Arnold open letter to supporters, Manchester United, 21 August 2023
evidence.text: Arnold said reintegration was one of several outcomes considered and planned, that the ultimate decision rested with him, his view evolved, strong opinions had arisen and he wanted to minimise distraction to club unity. He also described limits on the club’s investigation and third-party cooperation. This shows club agency and acknowledges public opinion among several factors; it does not establish press coverage as sole or legally compelled cause.

evidence.label: Greenwood statement reproduced with the official club decision, 21 August 2023
evidence.text: Greenwood denied doing what he was accused of, accepted making mistakes in his relationship and responsibility for circumstances leading to social media posts, and described the decision to continue his career away from United as collaborative between himself, his family and the club. This is his response, not a court finding.

evidence.label: Manchester United official loan announcement, 1 September 2023
evidence.text: United announced Greenwood signed for Getafe on a season-long loan, subject to international clearance; it described the move as enabling him to begin rebuilding his career away from Manchester United. It verifies the destination and form of move, not the cause of the earlier decision.

evidence.label: Getafe official announcement of one-season loan
evidence.text: Getafe announced an agreement with Manchester United for Greenwood to arrive on loan for one season.

evidence.label: The Guardian report on United’s decision, 21 August 2023

evidence.label: Sky News report on United decision, 21 August 2023

It also uses “cleared” in a video slug although the legal event was CPS discontinuance, not a verdict.

evidence.label: Nigel Farage and Reform UK: political-finance scrutiny · source audit
evidence.text: Political finance has a strong public-interest claim: these reports concern a political leader’s large donor relationship, election funding and alleged concealment. The April personal-gift disclosure and September undercover investigation are separate episodes. Parliamentary and police inquiries are not findings of guilt. The recovered sample is not a measure of total attention or proof that the university case received disproportionate coverage. The verified seven-day September sample contains five news reports, one institutional editorial and one official Channel 4 video, with search-only candidates excluded. O’Reilly’s seven-day sample contains two news reports and one opinion. These are different selected outlet samples, not complete or matched censuses. They show that political-finance scrutiny occurred, but cannot establish relative attention. Power over public decisions, electoral integrity, sums involved and credible new evidence support sustained scrutiny; a criminal conviction is not a prerequisite for public-interest reporting. Fair reporting must also preserve denials, distinguish suspicion from proof, and update outcomes.

evidence.label: BBC post-discontinuance coverage audit:25 unique page IDs
evidence.text: This verified sample establishes that BBC attention did continue well beyond 2 February 2023, through recurring, identifiable new hooks in 2023 and 2024 and a later 2026 Tottenham appointment controversy. It also shows that some stories merely recapped the dropped charges, while others explained the CPS test/reason; the 2 April 2026 report does the latter. A bounded publisher-page sample cannot establish that coverage lasted “too long,” compare proportionality against other cases or all football transfers, or resolve a racial-bias hypothesis. The only direct race-related framing evidence found here is attributed supporter-group commentary in the 28 March 2026 BBC report; do not infer identity from appearance or turn the source’s claim into a finding. The page count is not the event count. Multiple distinct pages can cover the same underlying event (e.g. 2 April 2026 interview/apology); AV derivatives and liveblog posts must not be inflated into standalone articles. Some pages are transfer gossip/audience formats rather than independently reported Greenwood coverage.

context.statusAtWindowEnd: CPS discontinued the criminal proceedings on 2 February 2023; no trial or not-guilty verdict occurred. Greenwood denied the charges. Manchester United later conducted a separate internal employer investigation and announced a mutually agreed departure away from Old Trafford on 21 August 2023. United’s CEO said the final decision rested with him, he had considered reintegration among several outcomes, and he took strong opinions and potential distraction into account. United announced a season-long Getafe loan on 1 September. The sequence does not establish that press coverage alone forced a move abroad. Later context: BBC reported a permanent Marseille deal on 18 July 2024, with an official Marseille player profile confirming he joined that club; this is separate from the 2023 Getafe loan.

legalOutcomeContext.procedure: All criminal charges discontinued2February2023; no trial, conviction, acquittal or not-guilty verdict.

legalOutcomeContext.departure: Club/player described a mutually agreed career away from Old Trafford;1September Getafe loan is documented. Reported backlash is one possible influence, not proof that the press alone forced exile.
legalOutcomeContext.care: Neither a witness withdrawal nor a continuing relationship establishes truth, falsity, consent or the reason for withdrawal. Do not speculate about witness motives. Police explicitly encouraged potential victims to seek help. No measured deterrent effect is established by this inventory.
legalOutcomeContext.racialPattern: A defensible initial story does not settle whether selection, repeated framing, prominence and persistence produce unequal treatment. Structural bias can be examined without an editor admitting intent. A deliberate strategy to conceal bias is a separate claim requiring evidence. These selected cases do not by themselves measure a general disparity; combine specific wording and chronology with wider research and suitable comparisons. No recent matched UK comparator pile-on has been established here.

pileOnDefinition: A campaign of repeated, concentrated attention to one person over a defined period, assessed against substantiated new developments, public value, framing, proportionality and persistence. Critical reporting or backlash alone does not establish a pile-on. No universal article limit determines fairness.

representationResearch.title: When an individual story becomes a racial pattern
representationResearch.interpretation: A defensible initial story does not settle whether selection, repeated framing, prominence and persistence produce unequal treatment. Structural bias can be examined without an editor admitting intent. A deliberate strategy to conceal bias is a separate claim requiring evidence.

studies.label: Cardiff REACH media monitoring report (2011)
studies.text: Cardiff REACH report (2011): 66.9% of 499 sampled items featuring Black males aged11–24 were crime-related, compared with41.9% for all young men/boys, not white-only. Eight two-week monitoring windows,2008–09; news in print, TV and radio. Victims were included. This is historical content analysis, not a measure of the present cases or evidence of each editor’s intent.
studies.finding: Crime accounted for 66.9% of sampled items featuring Black young men and boys, against 41.9% for all young men and boys.
studies.limit: The comparator includes Black youth; the sample is from 2008–09 and includes victims. It does not mean 67% portrayed Black people as criminals.

studies.label: Black British Voices Project (2023)
studies.text: Cambridge/Voice/I-Cubed Black British Voices (2023), over10,000 respondents: three in four believed Black businesses were treated unfairly by investors and financial institutions. The report describes perceived media stereotyping and football double standards. Survey/interviews are evidence of respondents’ experiences and perceptions, not a content audit or a causal finding for these cases.
studies.finding: Three in four respondents believed Black businesses were treated unfairly by investors and financial institutions. Media stereotyping and football double standards were also concerns in the report.
studies.limit: A survey and interviews document reported experience and perceptions. Business-investment findings cannot be relabelled as a measured media-coverage disparity.
studies.locator: Business/enterprise and media chapters; University of Cambridge summary.

representationResearch.claimBoundary: Neither serious allegations nor proven wrongdoing gives an outlet unlimited permission for humiliation. Fair scrutiny of alleged abuse also protects complainants; the question is how the coverage treats evidence, power and people.
